Hi Jonas —

Per our contract were notifying you that Horizon will onboard a new analytics provider, DataLens, to process aggregated telemetry for our population health product. Expected go-live: 2027-05-12.

Attached: subprocessor_notification.pdf (contains scope, dataset types, and processing location). High-level notes:
- Type of processing: aggregated usage + anonymized event telemetry
- Data residency: US primary, EU customers routed to EU region only; DataLens will not export EU data to the US without SCCs or appropriate transfer mechanisms
- Security: DataLens supports AES-256 at rest, TLS1.2+ in transit; SOC 2 Type II report enclosed in a separate doc.

Can you confirm receipt and whether Redwood requires the 45-day notification window to start today, or if the parties can agree to a 30-day operative window for this vendor? Were happy to execute an addendum via DocuSign once we align on the objection process and any required redlines.

Thanks for the heads up and the portal link, received. Ive looped in Laura (legal) and Irene (privacy engineering) to help triage the security artifacts. Quick answers up front:
- Receipt confirmed
- Redwoods standard clause currently requires a 45-day notice for material subprocessors; we can consider a 30-day notice if Horizon accepts a defined, short objection window (we typically require 14 days from notice for objection and removal steps) and the vendor passes our security checklist.

Can you attach DataLenss SOC 2 report and a short statement confirming encryption of customer PII both at rest and in transit? Also: does DataLens do any cross-border processing for EU-origin records? If so, provide the mechanism (SCCs? adequacy?).

Im attaching a proposed one-page redline to the notification timing and objection language (redline_proposal.docx). If Horizon is comfortable with a 14-day objection resolution window and the listed controls, we can sign the addendum via DocuSign and target the May 12 date.

Next steps: please circulate SOC2 + encryption statement and confirm acceptance of the objection timeline by EOD Wednesday 2027-04-27. If we dont hear back well escalate to a 45-day default per contract.

—Jonas

Forwarding Michael's note and attachments for internal sign-off. Bottom line recommendations from Legal & Privacy after quick review: 

1) Accept onboarding contingent on the following redlines:
   - Keep effective notice window at 30 days but codify a 14-day objection window for Redwood to investigate and trigger removal rights; allow Horizon one 7-day remediation period if Horizon proposes documented mitigations in writing.
   - Explicitly require SCCs for any EU->US transfer; add an audit right to verify DataLenss EU cluster residency for Horizon accounts that opt-in to EU residency.
   - Add an encryption representation (AES-256 at rest, TLS1.2+ in transit) and a quarterly key rotation statement.

2) Technical checks required before go-live (Irene): confirm KV cache and telemetry pseudonymization steps, confirm no raw PII leaves EU cluster.

3) Operational: Procurement should require DocuSign envelope with addendum, redlined as discussed. We should avoid a permanent obligation to accept short remediation windows for high-severity control failures; if remediation fails, removal is required.

If we accept these redlines I recommend we respond to Michael that Redwood agrees and ask Horizon to send the DocuSign addendum with the incorporated redlines. I attached a draft clause (included as text in my reply) — please review.
